description: A trend-following strategy using two three-period moving averages—one calculated on the high and one on the low—to enter trades on pullbacks and exit on opposing average touches. The strategy includes adaptive stop-loss management by trailing stops candle-by-candle based on new highs in uptrends and new lows in downtrends. A longer moving average (e.g., 55-period) may be added to assist with trend direction filtering.
market_regime: Trending markets with clear directional bias
entry_rules: 1. Identify the trend (price above longer moving average or higher highs and higher lows for uptrend; price below longer moving average or lower highs and lower lows for downtrend). 2. For a buy: wait for a candle to close below the moving average calculated on the low, then enter long at the close. 3. For a sell: wait for a candle to close above the moving average calculated on the high, then enter short at the close.

exit_rules.description: Exit when price closes beyond the opposite moving average, and manage the position by trailing the stop according to candle structure.
exit_rules.stop_loss: Initial maximum stop loss recommended between 250–300 points. For longs, place stop below the low of the candle that triggers exit signal; for shorts, place stop above the high of the candle that triggers exit signal.
exit_rules.take_profit: No fixed take profit is defined. Trailing stop moves to the low of each candle that makes a new high in an uptrend, and to the high of each candle that makes a new low in a downtrend, until hit.

risk_management.position_sizing: Use a fixed maximum stop (e.g., 250–300 points) to size positions so that the loss does not exceed predetermined account risk per trade.

examples: Buy after a candle closes below the 3-period low average, then exit after a close above the 3-period high average with trailing stop yielding ~670 points.
Sell after a candle closes above the 3-period high average, trail stop on new lows until exit.
notes: The setup is adaptive and allows modification of moving averages, stop size, and additional filters. Success depends on proper trend reading; results may be poor in choppy or sideways markets.
